source.text: Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα ἦλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν, ὅπου ἦν Λάζαρος, ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν Ἰησοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: The therefore Jesus before six days of the Passover came to Bethany, where was Lazarus, whom raised out of dead [ones] Jesus.

en.L: So Jesus, six days before the Passover, came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from [the] dead.
en.B: Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus arrived in Bethany, where Lazarus was, the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
en.R: Six days before the Passover festival, Jesus came to Bethany. Lazarus was there, the man Jesus had raised from the dead.

es.L: Jesús, pues, seis días antes de la Pascua, vino a Betania, donde estaba Lázaro, a quien Jesús había resucitado de [los] muertos.
es.B: Seis días antes de la Pascua, Jesús llegó a Betania, donde estaba Lázaro, el hombre a quien Jesús había resucitado de entre los muertos.
es.R: Seis días antes de la fiesta de la Pascua, Jesús fue a Betania. Allí estaba Lázaro, el hombre a quien Jesús había resucitado.

fr.L: Jésus donc, six jours avant la Pâque, vint à Béthanie, où était Lazare, que Jésus avait ressuscité des morts.
fr.B: Six jours avant la Pâque, Jésus arriva donc à Béthanie, où se trouvait Lazare, l’homme que Jésus avait ressuscité des morts.
fr.R: Six jours avant la fête de la Pâque, Jésus est arrivé à Béthanie. Lazare était là, l’homme que Jésus avait ressuscité des morts.

sw.L: Basi Yesu, siku sita kabla ya Pasaka, alifika Bethania, alikokuwa Lazaro, ambaye Yesu alimfufua kutoka kwa wafu.
sw.B: Kisha, siku sita kabla ya Pasaka, Yesu alifika Bethania, alikokuwa Lazaro, yule mtu ambaye Yesu alikuwa amemfufua kutoka kwa wafu.
sw.R: Siku sita kabla ya sikukuu ya Pasaka, Yesu alikuja Bethania. Lazaro alikuwa huko, yule mtu ambaye Yesu alikuwa amemfufua kutoka kwa wafu.

vi.L: Vậy sáu ngày trước Lễ Vượt Qua, Đức Giê-xu đến Bê-tha-ni, nơi La-xa-rơ ở, người mà Đức Giê-xu đã khiến sống lại từ [cõi] chết.
vi.B: Sáu ngày trước Lễ Vượt Qua, Đức Giê-xu đến Bê-tha-ni, nơi La-xa-rơ ở; đó là người Đức Giê-xu đã khiến sống lại từ cõi chết.
vi.R: Sáu ngày trước Lễ Vượt Qua, Đức Giê-xu đến Bê-tha-ni. La-xa-rơ ở đó. Đó là người Đức Giê-xu đã cho sống lại từ cõi chết.

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서는 유월절 엿새 전에 베다니에 가셨다. 그곳에는 나사로가 있었는데, 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살리신 사람이었다.
ko.B: 유월절 엿새 전에 예수께서 베다니에 오셨다. 그곳에는 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살리신 나사로가 있었다.
ko.R: 유월절 명절 엿새 전에 예수께서 베다니에 오셨다. 거기에는 나사로가 있었다. 나사로는 예수께서 죽음에서 다시 살리신 사람이었다.

pt.L: Então Jesus, seis dias antes da Páscoa, veio a Betânia, onde estava Lázaro, a quem Jesus ressuscitou dentre [os] mortos.
pt.B: Então, seis dias antes da Páscoa, Jesus chegou a Betânia, onde estava Lázaro, o homem que Jesus tinha ressuscitado dentre os mortos.
pt.R: Seis dias antes da festa da Páscoa, Jesus foi a Betânia. Lázaro estava lá, o homem que Jesus tinha ressuscitado dos mortos.

am.L: ስለዚህ ኢየሱስ ከፋሲካ ስድስት ቀን በፊት ወደ ቢታንያ መጣ፤ በዚያም ኢየሱስ ከሙታን ያስነሣው አልዓዛር ነበረ።
am.B: ከዚያም ከፋሲካ ስድስት ቀን በፊት ኢየሱስ ወደ ቢታንያ ደረሰ፤ በዚያም ኢየሱስ ከሙታን ያስነሣው አልዓዛር ነበረ።

hi.L: इसलिए यीशु फ़सह से छह दिन पहले बैतनिय्याह में आए, जहाँ लाज़र था, जिसे यीशु ने मरे हुओं में से जिलाया था।
hi.B: फिर फ़सह से छह दिन पहले यीशु बैतनिय्याह पहुँचे, जहाँ लाज़र था, वही आदमी जिसे यीशु ने मरे हुओं में से जिलाया था।
hi.R: फ़सह के पर्व से छह दिन पहले यीशु बैतनिय्याह आए। लाज़र वहीं था, वह आदमी जिसे यीशु ने मरे हुओं में से जिला उठाया था।

ru.L: Итак Иисус за шесть дней до Пасхи пришёл в Вифанию, где был Лазарь, которого воскресил из мёртвых Иисус.
ru.B: За шесть дней до Пасхи Иисус пришёл в Вифанию, где был Лазарь, тот, кого Иисус воскресил из мёртвых.
ru.R: За шесть дней до праздника Пасхи Иисус пришёл в Вифанию. Там был Лазарь, которого Иисус воскресил из мёртвых.

uk.L: Тож Ісус за шість днів до Пасхи прийшов у Віфанію, де був Лазар, якого Ісус підняв із мертвих.
uk.B: Тоді, за шість днів до Пасхи, Ісус прибув у Віфанію, де жив Лазар, той, кого Ісус воскресив із мертвих.
uk.R: За шість днів до свята Пасхи Ісус прийшов у Віфанію. Там був Лазар, якого Ісус воскресив із мертвих.

ja.L: そこでイエスは、過越祭の六日前に、ベタニアに来られた。そこには、イエスが死者[たち]の中から起こされたラザロがいた。
ja.B: さて、過越祭の六日前に、イエスはベタニアに着かれた。そこには、イエスが死者の中からよみがえらせられたラザロがいた。
ja.R: 過越祭の六日前に、イエスはベタニアに来られました。そこには、イエスが死んだ人たちの中から生き返らせられたラザロがいました。

decisions.choice: where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised (SBLGNT)
alternatives: where Lazarus was, the one who had died, whom Jesus raised
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, among them most later ones, add "the one who had died" after Lazarus's name. Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, with other early witnesses, do not have the words. They add nothing new, since the next clause says Jesus raised him from the dead, and look like a copyist's explanation. A footnote gives the longer reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: six days before the Passover: the start of the last week before Jesus's death
decisions.reason: This is the Passover that was near in 11:55, the third John names (2:13; 6:4). Jesus dies at this festival, on the day of Preparation (19:14, 31). From here John counts down to it: the next day comes in 12:12, and 13:1 opens with "before the feast of the Passover". Bethany was about two miles from Jerusalem (11:18), close enough for pilgrims to stay there.

decisions.choice: So: the story picks up after the leaders' orders of 11:57
alternatives: a strong "therefore" giving the reason for his coming
decisions.reason: The little word links this scene loosely to what went before. The chief priests and Pharisees had ordered anyone who knew where Jesus was to report it (11:57), and he had withdrawn to Ephraim (11:54). Now, with the festival near, he comes back to a village close to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: whom Jesus raised: John names Jesus again at the end of the sentence
decisions.reason: The sentence already began with Jesus as its subject, yet John repeats the name at the end, so that the man Lazarus is tied firmly to the one who raised him. That raising is what brings the crowds in verse 9 and the plot in verse 10.

decisions.choice: the man Jesus had raised (B, R); Lazarus was there (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the repeated name (meaning decision m4) and use "had raised", since the raising came before this visit. Readable makes two sentences and adds "festival" to Passover so a young reader knows what it was.

decisions.choice: el hombre a quien (B, R); Allí estaba Lázaro (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: makes plain who Lazarus is.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense (12:4 "dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (12:1-11). The passé simple ("vint", "arriva") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus est arrivé"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé. The imperfect ("servait", "emportait", "croyaient") is used at every level for what was going on or kept happening, and the pluperfect "avait ressuscité" for the raising, which came before this visit (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic
alternatives: capitalised pronouns, as the English setting offers
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns for Jesus are written as for anyone else.

decisions.choice: "которого воскресил из мёртвых Иисус" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the name at the end of the sentence, where John repeats it (meaning decision m4); Balanced and Readable use the ordinary order.

decisions.choice: "підняв із мертвих" (L); "воскресив" (B, R)
decisions.reason: *egeirō* is the ordinary verb for raising up; Literal keeps that picture, Balanced and Readable use the usual Ukrainian word for raising the dead. So also in 12:9 and 12:17.

decisions.choice: "起こされた" (L); "よみがえらせられた" (B); "生き返らせられた" (R)
decisions.reason: The narrator's light respect form for Jesus's action is kept, also on the causative verb. Literal keeps the Greek picture "raised" (起こす); Balanced and Readable say "brought back to life". Every level repeats Jesus's name at the end, as the Greek does (m4).

source.text: ἐποίησαν οὖν αὐτῷ δεῖπνον ἐκεῖ, καὶ ἡ Μάρθα διηκόνει, ὁ δὲ Λάζαρος εἷς ἦν ἐκ τῶν ἀνακειμένων σὺν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: Made therefore for him a dinner there, and the Martha was serving, the but Lazarus one was of the [ones] reclining with him;

en.L: So they made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a dinner there, and Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining [at table] with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: So they gave a dinner for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} there. Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of the guests who reclined at table with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: There they held a dinner for Jesus. Martha served the food, and Lazarus was one of the guests eating with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Le hicieron, pues, allí una cena, y Marta servía, y Lázaro era uno de los que estaban reclinados [a la mesa] con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Allí {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ofrecieron una cena. Marta servía, y Lázaro era uno de los que estaban a la mesa con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Allí hicieron una cena en honor de Jesús. Marta servía la comida, y Lázaro era uno de los que comían con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} firent donc là un dîner, et Marthe servait, et Lazare était l’un de ceux qui étaient allongés [à table] avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: On donna donc là un dîner en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} honneur. Marthe servait, et Lazare était parmi les convives allongés à table avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Là, on a préparé un repas en l’honneur de Jésus. Marthe servait à manger, et Lazare était parmi les invités qui mangeaient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Basi wakamwandalia chakula cha jioni huko, na Martha alikuwa akihudumu, na Lazaro alikuwa mmoja wa wale walioketi [mezani] pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.B: Basi walimwandalia chakula cha jioni huko. Martha alihudumu, na Lazaro alikuwa mmoja wa wageni walioketi mezani pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Huko walimfanyia Yesu karamu ya chakula cha jioni. Martha aliwahudumia chakula, na Lazaro alikuwa mmoja wa wageni waliokuwa wakila pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

vi.L: Vậy người ta làm tiệc tối đãi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở đó, và Ma-thê phục vụ, còn La-xa-rơ là một trong những người ngả mình [bên bàn ăn] cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Tại đó, người ta đãi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một bữa tối. Ma-thê lo phục vụ, còn La-xa-rơ là một trong những người cùng ngồi bàn với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ở đó, người ta làm một bữa tiệc tối để đãi Đức Giê-xu. Ma-thê dọn thức ăn, còn La-xa-rơ là một trong những người khách cùng ăn với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그래서 사람들이 거기서 그분께 저녁 식사를 베풀었는데, 마르다는 시중들고 있었고, 나사로는 그분과 함께 [식탁에] 기대어 앉은 사람들 가운데 하나였다.
ko.B: 그래서 사람들이 그곳에서 예수를 위하여 저녁 잔치를 열었다. 마르다는 시중을 들었고, 나사로는 그분과 함께 식탁에 기대어 앉은 손님들 가운데 하나였다.
ko.R: 그곳 사람들은 예수님을 위해 저녁 잔치를 열었다. 마르다는 음식을 날랐고, 나사로는 예수님과 함께 음식을 먹는 손님들 가운데 있었다.

pt.L: Então {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} fizeram ali um jantar, e Marta servia, e Lázaro era um dos que estavam reclinados [à mesa] com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.
pt.B: Ali ofereceram um jantar em {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} honra. Marta servia, e Lázaro era um dos convidados que estavam reclinados à mesa com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.
pt.R: Ali fizeram um jantar para Jesus. Marta servia a comida, e Lázaro era um dos convidados que estavam comendo com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

am.L: ስለዚህ በዚያ ራት አዘጋጁለት፤ ማርታም ታገለግል ነበር፤ አልዓዛርም ከእርሱ ጋር [በማዕድ] ከተደገፉት አንዱ ነበረ።
am.B: ስለዚህ በዚያ ራት አዘጋጁለት። ማርታ ታስተናግድ ነበር፤ አልዓዛርም ከእርሱ ጋር በማዕድ ከተቀመጡት እንግዶች አንዱ ነበረ።

hi.L: तब [लोगों] ने वहाँ उनके लिए भोज तैयार किया, और मार्था सेवा कर रही थी, और लाज़र उनमें से एक था जो उनके साथ [भोजन पर] टेक लगाए बैठे थे।
hi.B: तब वहाँ लोगों ने उनके लिए भोज दिया। मार्था परोस रही थी, और लाज़र उन मेहमानों में से एक था जो उनके साथ भोजन पर टेक लगाए बैठे थे।
hi.R: वहाँ लोगों ने यीशु के लिए भोज रखा। मार्था खाना परोस रही थी, और लाज़र भी उन मेहमानों में था जो यीशु के साथ खाना खा रहे थे।

ru.L: Итак, сделали {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} там ужин, и Марфа прислуживала, а Лазарь был одним из возлежавших [за столом] с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.
ru.B: Там для {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} устроили ужин. Марфа прислуживала, а Лазарь был среди гостей, возлежавших за столом вместе с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.
ru.R: Там для Иисуса устроили ужин. Марфа подавала еду, а Лазарь был среди гостей, которые ели вместе с {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.

uk.L: Тож зробили {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}} там вечерю, і Марта прислуговувала, а Лазар був одним із тих, що возлежали з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.
uk.B: Тож там улаштували для {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} вечерю. Марта прислуговувала, а Лазар був серед гостей, які сиділи з {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}} до столу.
uk.R: Там для Ісуса влаштували вечерю. Марта подавала їжу, а Лазар був серед гостей, що їли разом із {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}.

ja.L: そこで人々は、そこで[イエス]のために夕食を用意した。そしてマルタは給仕をしていた。ラザロは、[イエス]と共に[食卓に]横になっている者たちの一人であった。
ja.B: 人々はそこでイエスのために夕食の席を設けた。マルタは給仕をし、ラザロは、イエスと共に食卓で身を横たえている客の一人であった。
ja.R: そこで人々は、イエスのために夕食会を開きました。マルタは料理を運んで、みんなの世話をしました。ラザロは、イエスと一緒に食事をしている客の一人でした。

decisions.choice: they: the people of the house, not named
alternatives: the village of Bethany as a whole
decisions.reason: John does not say who gave the dinner or whose house it was. Martha serves and her sister and brother are present, which suggests the family took part. Mark and Matthew place a dinner at Bethany two days before the Passover in the house of Simon the leper (Mark 14:1-3; Matthew 26:2-6), and many see the same event there. John's account does not depend on settling this.

decisions.choice: was serving: waiting on the guests at table
alternatives: serving in a wider sense, as a disciple
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for serving food and waiting on guests. The tense pictures her busy through the meal, as in the other story about the two sisters (Luke 10:40). Jesus later uses the same word for anyone who serves him (12:26).

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on couches around a low table, as guests did at a formal meal
alternatives: sitting on chairs at a table
decisions.reason: At a festive meal guests lay on their left side on couches or cushions, leaning on the elbow, with their feet stretched out away from the table. This is why Mary can reach Jesus's feet in verse 3, and why the disciple whom Jesus loved can lean back against him at the last supper (13:23-25).

decisions.choice: Lazarus at table: the man raised from death eating with the one who raised him
decisions.reason: John notes that Lazarus was among the guests. The man who was four days in the tomb (11:39) now shares an ordinary meal, which shows that he is truly alive. It also explains the crowds who come to see him (verse 9).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "my" and "me" when Jesus speaks of himself (verses 7-8). At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: gave a dinner, reclined at table (B); held a dinner, eating with (R)
decisions.reason: "Made a dinner" is the Greek idiom; "gave" or "held" is the natural way to say it. Balanced keeps the posture of the guests, which verse 3 needs (meaning decision m3); Readable simply says they were eating together.

decisions.choice: reclinados [a la mesa] (L); a la mesa (B); comían (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the posture of a formal meal (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say what it meant.

decisions.choice: "On donna un dîner" (B); "on a préparé un repas" (R)
decisions.reason: John does not say who gave the dinner (meaning decision m1). French "on" leaves the hosts unnamed, as the Greek does, where "ils" with no one named before it would leave the reader looking for whom it means. Literal keeps the Greek plural "ils". "En son honneur" says what "made him a dinner" means.

decisions.choice: "ngả mình [bên bàn ăn]" (L); "ngồi bàn" (B); "cùng ăn" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the posture of guests at a formal meal; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Vietnamese way of saying someone ate at the table, since "nằm" would suggest lying down to sleep.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific -si- and 께서 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific third person ("उनके लिए", "उनके साथ") and by the forms of address, at every level, through this passage.

The Greek verb has an unnamed plural subject, the people of the house (meaning decision m1). Hindi "उन्होंने" would read as the honorific for Jesus himself, so every level says "people", bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}, {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}, {{deity_pronoun:ним|Ним}}, {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}}
decisions.reason: As in English, every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including the case forms Russian needs and "я" mid-sentence when Jesus speaks of himself (style guide sections 7 and 7b).

decisions.choice: "возлежавших [за столом]" (L); "возлежавших за столом" (B)
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a formal meal (meaning decision m3), and verse 3 needs the posture: Mary could reach his feet. Readable says simply that they ate with him.

decisions.choice: "[食卓に]横になっている" (L); "食卓で身を横たえている" (B); "一緒に食事をしている" (R)
decisions.reason: Guests at a formal meal lay on couches (m3), which is why Mary can reach Jesus's feet in verse 3; Literal and Balanced keep the posture, Readable says simply that they were eating together, as the English does.

en.L: So Mary, having taken a pound of perfumed oil of pure nard, very costly, anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfumed oil.
en.B: Then Mary took {{units:about 12 ounces|a Roman pound}} of very costly perfumed oil, pure nard, and anointed Jesus's feet and wiped {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her hair. The fragrance of the oil filled the house.

decisions.choice: a pound: a Roman pound, about 327 grams (about 11.5 ounces)
decisions.reason: The word is the Roman pound, lighter than the modern pound of 16 ounces. It is a large amount of perfume, far more than a person would use at one time, and it was worth about a year's wages (verse 5). John uses the same measure for the hundred pounds of spices Nicodemus brings for Jesus's burial (19:39).

decisions.choice: pure: genuine, unmixed nard
alternatives: a place or plant name, perhaps from the pistachio
decisions.reason: The adjective is found almost only here and in the same phrase in Mark 14:3, so its meaning is not certain. It most likely comes from the root for "faith" and "trust", giving "genuine" or "pure", nard that had not been mixed with cheaper oils. Some take it from the name of the pistachio tree or of a place, and others as "liquid". The sense "genuine" fits the stress on the oil's great cost. A footnote gives the other views.

decisions.choice: perfumed oil of nard: a costly fragrant oil from the nard plant
decisions.reason: The first word is perfumed oil, as in 11:2, which already refers to this anointing. Nard (spikenard) was an aromatic oil made from the root of a plant that grows in the Himalayas, imported from far away and very expensive. It is named in the Song of Songs as a precious perfume (Song of Songs 1:12; 4:13-14).

decisions.choice: anointing the feet and wiping them with her hair: an act of humble, lavish devotion
alternatives: the usual courtesy of a host to a guest
decisions.reason: A host might give a guest water for the feet or put a little oil on the head (Luke 7:44-46). Mary pours costly perfume on Jesus's feet and wipes them with her own hair. Caring for feet was the work of a slave, and a respectable woman did not usually let down her hair in company, so the act shows both humility and great love. Mark and Matthew say the woman poured the perfume on Jesus's head (Mark 14:3; Matthew 26:7); John tells of the feet. With so much perfume, both may have happened, but each writer tells what matters for his account. In John the scene looks ahead to Jesus washing his disciples' feet (13:4-5).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 12 ounces|a Roman pound}}
decisions.reason: A modern reader takes "a pound" as 16 ounces, so Balanced and Readable give the weight in ounces by default (meaning decision m1), and the units setting shows "a Roman pound". Literal keeps the ancient unit.

decisions.choice: perfumed oil, anointed (L, B); perfume, poured it on (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 11:2, which refers ahead to this anointing, so the two verses match at every level. Readable says plainly what anointing was here, as 11:2 does, and explains nard briefly.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 330 gramos|una libra romana}}
decisions.reason: A Roman pound, about 327 grams (meaning decision m1), rounded; the traditional measure is one tap away.

decisions.choice: ungió (L, B); lo derramó sobre (R)
decisions.reason: As in English.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 330 grammes|une livre romaine}}
decisions.reason: The French units setting is metric by default (French brief §7), where the English default is ounces. The Roman pound weighed about 327 grams (meaning decision m1), so "environ 330 grammes" gives the amount; a French "livre" is today half a kilo, so "une livre" alone would mislead. Literal keeps "une livre", the unit John names.

decisions.choice: "parfum" at every level; Readable adds "une huile qui sentait très bon"
decisions.reason: French "parfum" is the ordinary word for a costly fragrant preparation, oil included, and reads naturally twice in the sentence; "huile parfumée" is heavier and "onguent" suggests a cream. Readable says that it was an oil (meaning decision m3), as the English Readable does. 11:2 should use the same word.

decisions.choice: {{units:karibu gramu 330|ratili moja ya Kirumi}}
decisions.reason: A Roman pound was about 327 grams, as the meaning note says. The metric figure is the default and the original measure the alternative, as for the other measures in John; the English default is ounces. Literal keeps "ratili moja".

decisions.choice: "{{units:khoảng 330 gam|một lít-ra}}"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese readers use metric measures, so the default is grams and the alternative the original unit; Literal keeps "một lít-ra". This differs from the English US units.

decisions.choice: "dầu thơm cam tùng"
decisions.reason: "cam tùng" is the Vietnamese name of the nard plant; "dầu thơm" keeps it an oil, which "nước hoa" (modern perfume) would not.

decisions.choice: {{units:약 330그램|한 리트라}}: metric by default, the Roman pound as the alternative; Literal keeps "한 리트라"
decisions.reason: The Korean guide makes metric the default unit (section 7), unlike the English, which gives US units. The "되는" after the span lets both choices take the same grammar.

decisions.choice: {{units:cerca de 330 gramas|uma libra romana}}
decisions.reason: The Portuguese default is metric (style section 7), unlike the English ounces: a Roman pound was about 327 grams (meaning decision m1), rounded to 330. The units setting shows the original measure; Literal keeps "uma libra". "Perfume" (L, B, R) and "ungiu" (L, B) match 11:2, which refers ahead to this anointing.

decisions.choice: {{units:330 ግራም ያህል|አንድ የሮማ ሊትራ}}
decisions.reason: Amharic gives weights in metric units, so Balanced and Readable say about 330 grams (meaning decision: about 327 grams), and the units setting shows the Roman pound. Literal keeps the ancient unit, "ሊትራ".

decisions.choice: {{units:लगभग 330 ग्राम|एक रोमी पाउंड}}
decisions.reason: Hindi readers weigh in grams, so the default is metric where the English default is in ounces (meaning decision m1: about 327 grams); the alternative and Literal keep the Roman pound (style guide section 7). "पाउंड" alone would be taken as the modern pound, so the unit is called Roman.

decisions.choice: "जटामांसी" for nard
decisions.reason: "जटामांसी" is the Hindi name of the nard plant and its oil, as in Mark 14:3.

decisions.choice: {{units:около 330 граммов|римский фунт}}
alternatives: the US units of the English

decisions.choice: hand over: betray him to his enemies
alternatives: hand over, with no thought of betrayal
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71, the verb means to hand someone over. Used of Judas, one of Jesus's own disciples, it means betrayal (13:2, 21; 18:2-5).

decisions.choice: the one who was about to: what Judas would soon do
alternatives: the one who intended to, at this moment
decisions.reason: The participle looks ahead from the narrator's point of view, as in 6:71. It names Judas by the deed for which he is remembered; it does not say he had already decided on it at this dinner.

decisions.choice: Judas Iscariot (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts name Judas here as "son of Simon", as he is named in 6:71 and 13:2, 26. The shorter name is in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus and early papyri. A footnote gives the longer reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: one of his disciples: one of Jesus's own followers
decisions.reason: John stresses that the objection comes from inside the circle of disciples, as he did when he first named Judas (6:70-71). Mark and Matthew say some of those present, or the disciples, were angry (Mark 14:4; Matthew 26:8); John names the one who spoke.

decisions.choice: spoke up (B); spoke up ... He said (R)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This is the only such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:64 and 6:71 (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb; Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was. Readable names Jesus to make clear who would be betrayed.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: entregar (L); traicionar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the plain verb, which here means betray (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in the earlier chapters, for the whole of chapter 12.

decisions.choice: "Giu-đa", "ông ta" for Judas in the narrative
decisions.reason: Many Vietnamese versions call Judas "hắn", which condemns him in the pronoun itself; the narrator here uses neutral forms and lets the story judge him.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal (말한다); past at Balanced and Readable (말했다)
decisions.reason: John tells this event in the present tense; Literal keeps it, while Balanced and Readable use the past that Korean narrative expects (one decision for the passage).

decisions.choice: "ይላል" (says), present, at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's historic present, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "कहता है" (L); "बोल उठा", "कहा" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells the story in the present tense here; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable use the past, as Hindi stories are told. One note for the passage.

decisions.choice: "सौंपनेवाला" (L); "पकड़वानेवाला" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain sense of the verb, "hand over"; Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was, with the word Matthew uses for it ("पकड़वाना", to have someone arrested).

decisions.choice: "Говорит" (L); "заговорил", "сказал" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Russian stories normally are. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "предать"
decisions.reason: Russian "предать" keeps both the plain sense of the verb (to hand over) and the betrayal (meaning decision m1), so one word serves every level.

decisions.choice: "言う" (L), "口を開いた" (B), "口をはさみました……言いました" (R); "引き渡そうとしていた" (L), "裏切ることになる" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's present of storytelling, the only one in this passage; Balanced and Readable tell it in the past. Literal keeps the plain sense "hand over", and Balanced and Readable say what Judas's handing over was (m1).

alignments.target_span: for {{units:about a year's wages|three hundred denarii}}

decisions.choice: three hundred denarii: about a year's wages
decisions.reason: A denarius was a silver coin, the usual pay for a laborer's day of work (Matthew 20:2). Three hundred denarii was the pay for about a year of working days, once Sabbaths and festivals are left out. Philip reckoned that two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for the crowd (6:7); this perfume was worth more. Mark has "more than three hundred denarii" (Mark 14:5).

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor, especially at Passover
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:7-11) and a custom of the Passover season. At the last supper some disciples thought Judas had gone out to give something to the poor (13:29).

decisions.choice: Why ... not: a question that is really a complaint
alternatives: a real request for an explanation
decisions.reason: The question blames Mary for wasting the perfume. Jesus answers it as a rebuke when he says "Leave her" (verse 7), and the narrator gives Judas's true motive in verse 6.

decisions.choice: {{units:about a year's wages|three hundred denarii}} (B); {{units:about a year's pay|three hundred denarii}} (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:7: the coin means nothing to most readers, so Balanced and Readable give its value in wages by default, and the units setting shows "three hundred denarii". Literal always keeps the coin. The number stays in words, as in 6:7.

decisions.choice: the money given to the poor
decisions.reason: It was the money from the sale, not the oil, that would have gone to the poor; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: {{units:el salario de un año|trescientos denarios}}
decisions.reason: As at 6:7: the value in a year's wages (meaning decision m1), with the coin one tap away.

decisions.choice: "ba trăm đơ-ni-ê" (L, and the alternative in B, R); "khoảng một năm tiền công" (B, R default)
decisions.reason: "đơ-ni-ê" is the established Protestant transliteration of the Roman coin; the setting gives its value in a worker's wages.

decisions.choice: {{units:일 년 품삯쯤|300데나리온}}; Literal keeps "삼백 데나리온"
decisions.reason: The value is given in a modern measure by default and the Greek sum as the alternative, as the units setting does; the following particle (에, 은) fits both choices.

records.literal_gloss: Said but this not that about the poor it was a care to him, but that a thief he was and the money box having the [things] being put in he was carrying off.

en.L: But he said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, he used to carry off what was put into it.
en.B: He said this, not out of any care for the poor, but because he was a thief. He was in charge of the money box, and he used to take for himself what people put in it.
en.R: Judas did not say this because he cared about poor people. He said it because he was a thief. He was in charge of the group's money box, and he often stole the money people put in it.

es.L: Pero dijo esto, no porque le importaran los pobres, sino porque era ladrón, y teniendo la bolsa, se llevaba lo que se echaba en ella.
es.B: Dijo esto no porque le importaran los pobres, sino porque era ladrón. Tenía a su cargo la bolsa del dinero y se quedaba con lo que echaban en ella.
es.R: Judas no dijo esto porque le importaran los pobres. Lo dijo porque era ladrón. Estaba a cargo de la bolsa del dinero del grupo, y muchas veces robaba lo que la gente echaba en ella.

fr.L: Or il dit cela, non parce qu’il se souciait des pauvres, mais parce qu’il était voleur et, ayant la caisse, il emportait ce qu’on y mettait.
fr.B: Il dit cela, non par souci des pauvres, mais parce qu’il était voleur. Il tenait la caisse et prenait pour lui ce qu’on y déposait.
fr.R: Judas n’a pas dit cela parce qu’il pensait aux pauvres. Il l’a dit parce que c’était un voleur. Il gardait la caisse du groupe, et souvent il volait l’argent que les gens y mettaient.

sw.L: Lakini alisema hivi, si kwa sababu aliwajali maskini, bali kwa sababu alikuwa mwizi, na akiwa na mfuko wa fedha, alikuwa akichukua vile vilivyotiwa ndani yake.
sw.B: Alisema hivyo si kwa sababu aliwajali maskini, bali kwa sababu alikuwa mwizi. Yeye ndiye aliyeshika mfuko wa fedha, naye alikuwa akijichukulia kile watu walichotia ndani yake.
sw.R: Yuda hakusema hivyo kwa sababu aliwajali watu maskini. Alisema hivyo kwa sababu alikuwa mwizi. Yeye ndiye aliyeshika mfuko wa fedha wa kikundi, naye mara nyingi aliiba fedha ambazo watu walitia ndani yake.

vi.L: Nhưng ông ta nói điều này không phải vì quan tâm đến người nghèo, mà vì ông ta là kẻ trộm, và giữ túi tiền, ông ta thường lấy đi những gì [người ta] bỏ vào đó.
vi.B: Ông ta nói vậy không phải vì thương người nghèo, mà vì ông ta là kẻ trộm. Ông ta giữ túi tiền và thường lấy cho mình những gì người ta bỏ vào.
vi.R: Giu-đa nói vậy không phải vì thương người nghèo. Ông ta nói vậy vì ông ta là kẻ trộm. Ông ta giữ túi tiền chung của cả nhóm, và thường lấy cắp tiền người ta bỏ vào đó.

ko.L: 그런데 그가 이 말을 한 것은 가난한 사람들을 생각해서가 아니라, 그가 도둑이었고 돈주머니를 맡아 가지고 있으면서 거기에 넣은 것을 가져가곤 했기 때문이었다.
ko.B: 그가 이렇게 말한 것은 가난한 사람들을 걱정해서가 아니라, 그가 도둑이었기 때문이다. 그는 돈주머니를 맡고 있으면서, 사람들이 넣은 돈을 자기 것으로 빼내곤 했다.
ko.R: 유다가 이 말을 한 것은 가난한 사람들을 아껴서가 아니었다. 그는 도둑이었기 때문에 그렇게 말했다. 유다는 제자들의 돈주머니를 맡고 있었는데, 사람들이 넣은 돈을 자주 훔쳐 갔다.

pt.L: Mas ele disse isso não porque se importasse com os pobres, mas porque era ladrão e, tendo a bolsa do dinheiro, levava o que nela se punha.
pt.B: Ele disse isso não por se importar com os pobres, mas porque era ladrão. Ele cuidava da bolsa do dinheiro e costumava tirar para si o que se colocava nela.

am.B: ይህን ያለው ለድሆች ተቆርቁሮ አልነበረም፤ ሌባ ስለ ነበረ ነው። የገንዘቡን ሣጥን የሚይዘው እርሱ ነበረ፤ ሰዎች በውስጡ የሚያስቀምጡትንም ለራሱ ይወስድ ነበር።

hi.B: उसने यह ग़रीबों की किसी चिंता के कारण नहीं कहा, बल्कि इसलिए कि वह चोर था। पैसों की पेटी उसी के ज़िम्मे थी, और लोग जो उसमें डालते थे, उसमें से वह अपने लिए ले लेता था।
hi.R: यहूदा ने यह इसलिए नहीं कहा कि उसे ग़रीब लोगों की परवाह थी। उसने यह इसलिए कहा क्योंकि वह चोर था। चेलों के पैसों की पेटी उसी के पास रहती थी, और लोग जो पैसा उसमें डालते थे, उसमें से वह अक्सर चुरा लेता था।

ru.L: Сказал же он это не потому, что заботился о нищих, а потому, что был вор и, имея денежный ящик, уносил то, что туда клали.
ru.B: Он сказал это не из заботы о бедных, а потому, что был вором. У него хранился денежный ящик, и он брал себе то, что туда клали.
ru.R: Иуда сказал это не потому, что ему было дело до бедных. Он сказал так, потому что был вором. Он отвечал за общий денежный ящик учеников и часто крал деньги, которые туда клали.

uk.L: А сказав він це не тому, що дбав про бідних, але тому, що був злодій і, маючи скриньку, забирав те, що в неї клали.
uk.B: Він сказав це не з турботи про бідних, а тому, що був злодієм. Він відав скринькою для грошей і брав собі те, що в неї клали.
uk.R: Юда сказав це не тому, що турбувався про бідних людей. Він сказав так, бо був злодієм. Він відповідав за спільну скриньку з грошима і часто крав те, що люди туди клали.

ja.L: しかし彼がこう言ったのは、貧しい人々のことを心にかけていたからではなく、彼が盗人であって、金入れを預かっていながら、その中に入れられたものを持ち去っていたからである。
ja.B: 彼がこう言ったのは、貧しい人々のことを心にかけていたからではない。盗人だったからである。彼は金入れを預かっていて、その中に入れられたものを自分のものにしていた。
ja.R: ユダがこう言ったのは、貧しい人たちのことを心配していたからではありません。ユダはどろぼうだったのです。ユダは仲間のお金を入れる箱を任されていましたが、その中に入れられたお金を、たびたび盗んでいました。

decisions.choice: he said this, not because he cared: the narrator tells Judas's real motive
decisions.reason: John alone among the Gospels gives this comment. He writes looking back, knowing what Judas became, and shows that the concern for the poor was a cover.

decisions.choice: money box: the box in which the group's money was kept
decisions.reason: The word first meant a case for the mouthpieces of musical instruments and came to mean any box or case, especially one for money. Judas kept it for Jesus and the disciples (13:29). Gifts from supporters went into it, and money for food and for the poor came out of it.

decisions.choice: carry off: take away for himself, steal
alternatives: only carry, as the keeper of the box
decisions.reason: The verb means to carry or bear, and can also mean to carry off or take away, as in 20:15, where Mary thinks someone has carried Jesus's body away. Since John has just called Judas a thief, the second sense is meant here: he carried the box, and he carried off what was in it. The tense shows that he did it habitually.

decisions.choice: a thief: the same word Jesus used for the thief who comes to steal
decisions.reason: In 10:1, 8, 10 the thief is the one who comes only to steal and destroy, in contrast to the good shepherd. John uses the same word of Judas, the disciple who will hand the shepherd over.

decisions.choice: used to carry off (L); used to take for himself (B); often stole (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of stealing (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "carry" with "off", which still shows the verb's picture; Readable says plainly that he stole.

decisions.choice: was in charge of (B, R); the group's (R)
decisions.reason: "Having the money box" means he kept the group's money (13:29). Balanced and Readable say so; Readable adds whose money it was.

decisions.choice: se llevaba (L); se quedaba con (B); robaba (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: from the bare verb to what it meant (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: la caisse (L, B); la caisse du groupe (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a box or case for money (meaning decision m2). "La bourse" is the traditional word but today suggests a purse or the stock exchange; "la caisse" is the plain French word for the box where a group keeps its money. The same word is used in 13:29.

decisions.choice: 돈주머니 (the group's purse)
decisions.reason: 돈주머니 is the everyday word for a common purse and reads naturally at every level; the Greek word means a box for money, which the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: a bolsa do dinheiro; levava (L); tirar para si (B); roubava (R)
decisions.reason: "Bolsa" is the usual Portuguese word for a common purse, the group's money (meaning decision m2). Literal "levava" keeps the verb's picture of carrying and also means taking away; Balanced and Readable say plainly that he stole (meaning decision m3).
The Greek word is a box for keeping money (meaning decision m2), not a bag, so Hindi says "पेटी". The same word returns in 13:29.

decisions.choice: "уносил" (L); "брал себе" (B); "крал" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means carrying something away for oneself here (meaning decision m3); "носил" would say only that he carried the box.

decisions.choice: "盗人" (L, B), "どろぼう" (R); "持ち去っていた" (L), "自分のものにしていた" (B), "盗んでいました" (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense of stealing (m3), Literal keeping the picture of carrying off. 盗人 is the same word Japanese should use for the thief of 10:1-10 (m4); Readable uses the everyday どろぼう.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus, "Leave her, so that for the day of the burial-preparation of me she may keep it;

en.L: So Jesus said, "Let her be, in order that she may keep it for the day of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} preparation for burial.
en.B: Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She was to keep it for the day when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body is prepared for burial.
en.R: Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She was meant to keep this perfume for the day when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body is made ready to be buried.

fr.B: Jésus dit : « Laisse-la. Elle devait garder ce parfum pour le jour où {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps sera préparé pour la sépulture.
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Laisse-la tranquille. Ce parfum, elle devait le garder pour le jour où on préparera {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} corps pour l’enterrer.

sw.L: Basi Yesu akasema, "Mwache, ili ayaweke kwa ajili ya siku ya kuandaliwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kwa maziko.

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy để cô ấy yên, để cô ấy giữ dầu này cho ngày tẩm liệm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy để cô ấy yên. Cô ấy giữ dầu thơm này là để dành cho ngày thân thể {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} được chuẩn bị để đem chôn.

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그 여자를 가만두어라. 내 장례를 준비하는 날을 위하여 그 여자가 그것을 간직하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그 여자를 가만두어라. 이 향유는 내 몸을 장례 지낼 준비를 하는 날을 위해 그 여자가 간직해 둔 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "그 여자를 그냥 두어라. 이 여자는 이 향유를 간직해 두었다가, 내 몸을 묻으려고 준비하는 날에 쓰게 되어 있었다.

pt.L: Então Jesus disse: "Deixe-a, para que ela o guarde para o dia da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} preparação para o sepultamento.
pt.B: Jesus disse: "Deixe-a em paz. Ela devia guardá-lo para o dia em que o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo for preparado para o sepultamento.
pt.R: Jesus disse: "Deixe-a em paz. Ela tinha de guardar este perfume para o dia em que o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} corpo for preparado para ser enterrado.

ru.L: Итак, сказал Иисус: «Оставь её, чтобы она сохранила это ко дню {{deity_pronoun:моего|Моего}} приготовления к погребению.

uk.L: Тож Ісус сказав: «Залиш її, щоб вона зберегла це на день {{deity_pronoun:мого|Мого}} приготування до поховання.

decisions.choice: she was to keep it for the day of my burial: she did not sell it, and her anointing now is part of preparing his body for burial
alternatives: Let her keep the rest of it for the day of my burial
Let her alone, so that she may keep the memory of this for the day of my burial
decisions.reason: The Greek is brief and hard: "Leave her, so that for the day of my burial she may keep it." Since Mary has just used the perfume, "keep it" is puzzling. One reading takes the words as the purpose of her having kept it rather than selling it: it was kept for this, and by pouring it out now she prepares his body for burial ahead of time, as Mark says (Mark 14:8). A second reading supposes that only part was used, and Jesus tells them to let her keep the rest for his burial; but John says nothing of a remainder, and the women do not anoint his body in John (19:39-40). A third takes "it" as the memory of what she did. The first fits the context best, but the evidence is evenly balanced. A footnote gives the other readings.

decisions.choice: so that she may keep it (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "she has kept it for the day of my burial", without "so that", which is easier to understand. The harder wording is in early papyri, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, and the easier one looks like a correction. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: burial: preparing a body for burial
decisions.reason: The noun means the laying out and preparing of a body for the tomb, with spices and wrappings. John uses the related verb of what Joseph and Nicodemus did for Jesus's body, "as is the custom of the Jews to prepare for burial" (19:40). Mary's act looks ahead to his death, now close (12:23-24).

decisions.choice: Leave her: let her alone, stop troubling her
decisions.reason: The command answers Judas's complaint: Jesus defends Mary and tells the objectors to stop finding fault with her, as in Mark 14:6.

decisions.choice: She was to keep it (B); She was meant to keep (R)
alternatives: so that she may keep it (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow meaning decision m1: the perfume was kept for this purpose. "Was to keep" keeps the sense of purpose without following the variant "she has kept it". Literal keeps the Greek purpose clause and its ambiguity.

decisions.choice: my preparation for burial (L); my body is prepared for burial (B); my body is made ready to be buried (R)
decisions.reason: The noun means the preparing of a body, not only the burial (meaning decision m3); every level says so.

decisions.choice: "Laisse-la" (tu), then "vous" in verse 8
decisions.reason: The command is singular in Greek, spoken to Judas, who raised the complaint (meaning decision m4); in verse 8 Jesus turns to all of them with a plural. French can show both, so "laisse" here and "vous" in the next sentence.

decisions.choice: ensevelissement (L); mon corps sera préparé pour la sépulture (B, R)
decisions.reason: The noun means preparing a body for the tomb, not the burial itself (meaning decision m3). French "ensevelissement" (wrapping a body for burial) says exactly that in one word at Literal; Balanced and Readable spell it out, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nói" for Jesus speaking, at every level
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice (docs/vietnamese-style.md), settled in October 2026: the narrator introduces Jesus's words with the everyday verb, as it does for every other speaker, so the narrative stays modern and the three levels agree; "phán", the reverential verb, is kept for God speaking (1:33; 9:29; 12:28).

decisions.choice: Deixe-a (singular, você)
decisions.reason: The Greek command is singular, spoken to Judas, so Jesus uses the "você" form "deixe", as he speaks to any one person (style section 4).

decisions.choice: "ተዋት" (leave her, singular)
decisions.reason: The Greek command is singular, spoken to Judas, and Amharic marks the number of the one addressed, so it stays singular; in the next sentence Jesus speaks to all of them ("እናንተ").

decisions.choice: "Оставь" (singular)
decisions.reason: The Greek imperative is singular: Jesus answers Judas. Russian must choose a number, and the singular follows the Greek.

decisions.choice: "取っておくことになっていた" (B); "取っておくはずだった" (R); "取っておくためである" (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow m1: the perfume was kept for this purpose, without following the variant "she has kept it". Literal keeps the Greek purpose clause and its difficulty. decisions.choice: the poor you always have: an echo of Deuteronomy 15:11
decisions.reason: The law says that the poor will never cease from the land, and therefore commands Israel to open its hand to them (Deuteronomy 15:11). Jesus does not set aside that command; he says that there will always be time to help the poor.

decisions.choice: me you do not always have: Jesus will soon go away by his death
alternatives: a claim that he matters more than the poor
decisions.reason: The contrast is one of time. Jesus has said he will be with them only a little longer (7:33; 13:33). Mary's gift fits the short time that is left before his death (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the verse is part of the text (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and the Sinaitic Syriac leave out the whole verse. Nearly all other manuscripts have it. Some think it was added from the same saying in Matthew 26:11 and Mark 14:7, but the evidence for it is strong. A footnote notes the omission. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: I will not always be with you
alternatives: me you do not always have (Literal)
you will not always have me
decisions.reason: "You do not always have me" means that Jesus will not be with them for long (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable say that directly and look to the future, which the present tense implies here. The pronoun "I" takes no setting.

decisions.choice: plural you
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from Judas to all at table, so "you" is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: les pauvres, vous [les] avez ... mais moi, vous ne m’avez pas
alternatives: vous avez toujours les pauvres avec vous, mais vous ne m’avez pas toujours
decisions.reason: Greek puts "the poor" and "me" first, setting them against each other. French keeps that order by setting each one at the head of its clause and taking it up with a pronoun ("les", "m’"); the first pronoun is not in the Greek, so it is bracketed.

decisions.choice: "các con" for Jesus addressing his disciples

hi.R: यहूदियों की एक बड़ी भीड़ को पता चला कि यीशु बैतनिय्याह में हैं, इसलिए वे वहाँ गए। वे यीशु को देखने आए, पर वे लाज़र को भी देखना चाहते थे, जिसे यीशु ने मरे हुओं में से जिलाया था।

ru.L: Итак, узнала большая толпа из иудеев, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} там, и пришли не ради Иисуса только, но чтобы увидеть и Лазаря, которого {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} воскресил из мёртвых.
ru.B: Когда большая толпа иудеев узнала, что Иисус там, люди пришли не только ради Иисуса: они хотели увидеть и Лазаря, которого {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} воскресил из мёртвых.
ru.R: Большая толпа иудеев узнала, что Иисус в Вифании, и люди пошли туда. Они пришли посмотреть на Иисуса, но хотели увидеть и Лазаря, которого Иисус воскресил из мёртвых.

uk.L: Тож великий натовп юдеїв довідався, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} там, і вони прийшли не лише через Ісуса, але щоб побачити й Лазаря, якого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} підняв із мертвих.
uk.B: Коли великий натовп юдеїв довідався, що Ісус там, вони прийшли не лише заради Ісуса: вони хотіли побачити й Лазаря, якого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} воскресив із мертвих.
uk.R: Великий натовп юдеїв дізнався, що Ісус у Віфанії, і люди пішли туди. Вони прийшли побачити Ісуса, але хотіли побачити й Лазаря, якого Ісус воскресив із мертвих.

ja.L: そこで、ユダヤ人たちの大勢の群衆が、[イエス]がそこにおられることを知って、やって来た。イエスのためだけでなく、[イエス]が死者[たち]の中から起こされたラザロをも見るためであった。
ja.B: イエスがそこにおられると知った大勢のユダヤ人の群衆が、やって来た。イエスのためだけではなく、イエスが死者の中からよみがえらせられたラザロにも会いたかったのである。
ja.R: 大勢のユダヤ人の群衆が、イエスがベタニアにおられることを知って、そこへやって来ました。イエスに会うためだけではありません。イエスが死んだ人たちの中から生き返らせられたラザロも見たかったのです。

decisions.choice: the Jews: Jewish people from Jerusalem and the area around it
decisions.reason: This crowd is not the authorities, who are named separately in verse 10 and plot against those who believe. They are people who, like the mourners of 11:19 and 11:45, came out from Jerusalem, two miles away (11:18), many of them pilgrims gathering for the Passover (11:55). Many of them came to believe (verse 11).

decisions.choice: a large crowd, without the article (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts have the article, "the large crowd", in an unusual position. The meaning is much the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: that he was there: the words as the crowd heard them
decisions.reason: Greek keeps the tense of the words that were reported, so the Greek says "that he is there". It is not the historic present of storytelling.

decisions.choice: to see Lazarus also: they came to see the sign for themselves
decisions.reason: The raising of Lazarus had made him famous. People came to see the living man as well as Jesus, and this crowd spreads the news when Jesus enters Jerusalem (12:17-18).

decisions.choice: a large crowd of the Jews (B); a big crowd of the Jews (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the people of Jerusalem and the crowds there (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the crowd present, as 11:45 does; no footnote is needed.

decisions.choice: Jesus was there (B); Jesus was in Bethany (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus for clarity; Readable also names the village, from verse 1.

decisions.choice: los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: The Jewish people of Jerusalem and the area around it, not the authorities, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: Juifs at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, first met in this passage. Here the word means Jewish people from Jerusalem and its area, not the authorities (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable keep "Juifs" too; the authorities are named separately in verse 10 as "les chefs des prêtres".

decisions.choice: Wayahudi at every level in this chapter
decisions.reason: As the English: here John means the Jewish people from Jerusalem and the country around, so every level says "Wayahudi". The authorities are named as such ("wakuu wa makuhani", verse 10).

decisions.choice: "यहूदियों" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people of Jerusalem and the area (meaning decision m1), not the authorities, so Balanced and Readable keep "यहूदी" as Literal does (docs/john-terms.md). The same in verse 11.

decisions.choice: "иудеи" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people of Jerusalem and the area (meaning decision m1), so every level keeps "иудеи", as docs/john-terms.md settles.

decisions.choice: "ユダヤ人たち" (L); "ユダヤ人" (B, R)
decisions.reason: This crowd is the people of Jerusalem and the pilgrims (m1), not the authorities, who are named in verse 10; so Balanced and Readable say ユダヤ人, here and in verse 11.

source.text: ἐβουλεύσαντο δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἀποκτείνωσιν, ὅτι πολλοὶ δι’ αὐτὸν ὑπῆγον τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἐπίστευον εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Planned but the chief priests that also the Lazarus they might kill, \v 11 because many on account of him were going away of the Jews and were believing in the Jesus.

en.L: But the chief priests planned that they might kill Lazarus also, \v 11 because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.
en.B: The chief priests, however, resolved to put Lazarus to death as well, \v 11 because on his account many of the Jews were leaving them and believing in Jesus.
en.R: So the leading priests made plans to kill Lazarus too. \v 11 They wanted him dead because many of the Jews were leaving them and believing in Jesus. Lazarus was the reason.

es.L: Pero los principales sacerdotes acordaron matar también a Lázaro, \v 11 porque por causa de él muchos de los judíos se iban y creían en Jesús.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes, sin embargo, decidieron matar también a Lázaro, \v 11 porque por causa de él muchos de los judíos los estaban dejando y creían en Jesús.
es.R: Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes hicieron planes para matar también a Lázaro. \v 11 Lo querían muerto porque muchos judíos los estaban dejando a ellos para creer en Jesús. Lázaro era la razón.

fr.L: Or les chefs des prêtres décidèrent de tuer aussi Lazare, \v 11 parce qu’à cause de lui beaucoup d’entre les Juifs s’en allaient et croyaient en Jésus.
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres, eux, résolurent de faire mourir Lazare aussi, \v 11 car, à cause de lui, beaucoup de Juifs les quittaient et croyaient en Jésus.
fr.R: Alors les chefs des prêtres ont fait des plans pour tuer Lazare, lui aussi. \v 11 Ils voulaient sa mort parce que beaucoup de Juifs les quittaient et croyaient en Jésus. C’était à cause de Lazare.

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani walifanya shauri wamwue Lazaro naye, \v 11 kwa sababu kwa ajili yake wengi wa Wayahudi walikuwa wakienda zao na kumwamini Yesu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo wakuu wa makuhani waliazimia kumwua Lazaro pia, \v 11 kwa sababu kwa ajili yake Wayahudi wengi walikuwa wakiwaacha na kumwamini Yesu.
sw.R: Basi viongozi wa makuhani walifanya mipango ya kumwua Lazaro pia. \v 11 Walitaka afe kwa sababu Wayahudi wengi walikuwa wakiwaacha na kumwamini Yesu. Lazaro ndiye aliyekuwa sababu.

vi.L: Nhưng các thầy tế lễ cả bàn mưu giết luôn cả La-xa-rơ, \v 11 vì cớ ông ấy mà nhiều người Do Thái đang bỏ đi và tin vào Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Tuy nhiên, các thầy tế lễ cả quyết định giết cả La-xa-rơ nữa, \v 11 vì nhờ ông mà nhiều người Do Thái đang bỏ họ để tin vào Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Vì thế, các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu lập kế hoạch giết luôn La-xa-rơ. \v 11 Họ muốn ông chết, vì nhiều người Do Thái đang bỏ họ mà tin vào Đức Giê-xu. Tất cả là vì La-xa-rơ.

ko.L: 그러나 대제사장들은 나사로도 죽이려고 의논했다. \v 11 그 사람 때문에 유대인들 가운데 많은 사람이 떠나가서 예수를 믿고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러자 대제사장들은 나사로까지 죽이기로 결의했다. \v 11 나사로 때문에 많은 유대인이 자기들을 떠나 예수를 믿게 되었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 대제사장들은 나사로도 죽이려고 계획을 세웠다. \v 11 많은 유대인들이 자기들을 떠나 예수님을 믿고 있었는데, 그것은 나사로 때문이었다.

pt.L: Mas os chefes dos sacerdotes decidiram matar também Lázaro, \v 11 porque por causa dele muitos dos judeus iam embora e criam em Jesus.
pt.B: Os chefes dos sacerdotes, porém, resolveram matar também Lázaro, \v 11 porque por causa dele muitos dos judeus os estavam deixando e passando a crer em Jesus.
pt.R: Então os chefes dos sacerdotes fizeram planos para matar Lázaro também. \v 11 Eles queriam a morte dele porque muitos dos judeus estavam deixando os chefes dos sacerdotes e crendo em Jesus. Lázaro era o motivo.

hi.L: पर प्रधान याजकों ने योजना बनाई कि लाज़र को भी मार डालें, \v 11 क्योंकि उसके कारण बहुत-से यहूदी जा रहे थे और यीशु पर विश्वास कर रहे थे।
hi.B: पर प्रधान याजकों ने ठान लिया कि लाज़र को भी मरवा डालें, \v 11 क्योंकि उसके कारण बहुत-से यहूदी उन्हें छोड़कर यीशु पर विश्वास कर रहे थे।
hi.R: इसलिए प्रधान याजकों ने लाज़र को भी मार डालने की योजना बनाई। \v 11 वे उसे मरवाना चाहते थे, क्योंकि बहुत-से यहूदी उन्हें छोड़कर यीशु पर विश्वास कर रहे थे। इसका कारण लाज़र ही था।

ru.L: Решили же старшие священники убить и Лазаря, \v 11 потому что из-за него многие из иудеев уходили и верили в Иисуса.
ru.B: Старшие священники тогда решили казнить и Лазаря, \v 11 потому что из-за него многие иудеи уходили от них и верили в Иисуса.
ru.R: Поэтому старшие священники решили убить и Лазаря. \v 11 Они хотели его смерти, потому что многие иудеи уходили от них и начинали верить в Иисуса. Причиной был Лазарь.

uk.L: А старші священники вирішили вбити й Лазаря, \v 11 бо через нього багато юдеїв відходили й вірили в Ісуса.
uk.B: Проте старші священники вирішили стратити й Лазаря, \v 11 бо через нього багато юдеїв відходили від них і вірили в Ісуса.
uk.R: Тож старші священники почали готувати план, як убити й Лазаря. \v 11 Вони хотіли його смерті, бо багато юдеїв залишали їх і вірили в Ісуса. І причиною цього був Лазар.

ja.L: しかし、祭司長たちは、ラザロも殺そうと協議した。\v 11 彼のために、ユダヤ人たちのうちの多くの者が去って行き、イエスを信じるようになっていたからである。
ja.B: そこで祭司長たちは、ラザロも殺そうと決めた。\v 11 ラザロのことで、多くのユダヤ人が祭司長たちから離れて行き、イエスを信じるようになっていたからである。
ja.R: そこで祭司長たちは、ラザロも殺す計画を立てました。\v 11 ラザロのせいで、多くのユダヤ人が祭司長たちから離れて、イエスを信じるようになっていたからです。

decisions.choice: were going away: leaving the authorities and their way, to follow Jesus
alternatives: going off to Bethany to see Jesus and Lazarus
decisions.reason: The verb means to go away or depart. It can simply describe people going out from Jerusalem to Bethany, as the crowd did (verse 9). But the authorities are alarmed, and the verb is joined to "believing", so it most likely means that people were leaving them and their leadership, as some disciples "went back" from Jesus in 6:66. The other sense remains possible. A footnote gives it.

decisions.choice: the Jews: Jewish people of Jerusalem, as in verse 9
decisions.reason: These are people who were turning to Jesus, set against the chief priests. The word means the people, not their leaders.

decisions.choice: the chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families; Lazarus also, as well as Jesus
decisions.reason: The council had already decided to kill Jesus (11:53). Now the chief priests plan to kill Lazarus too, since he is the living proof of the sign that is drawing people to Jesus. The leading priests were mostly Sadducees, who denied that the dead rise (Acts 23:8), though John does not give that as their reason.

decisions.choice: were going away and believing: something going on and spreading
decisions.reason: Both verbs are in the imperfect: people kept leaving and coming to believe in Jesus, one after another. The key term is believe "in" Jesus (3:16; 11:45).

decisions.choice: leaving them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow meaning decision m1 and say whom the people were leaving: the authorities. Literal keeps the open "going away". This choice is uncertain; the footnote on m1 gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: leading priests
decisions.reason: As in 7:45 and 11:47, Readable says "leading priests", which a young reader can follow, and adds that Lazarus was the reason, which Balanced keeps as "on his account".

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R); los principales sacerdotes (L)
decisions.reason: As in John 7 and 11.

decisions.choice: los judíos (every level)
decisions.reason: The Jewish people of Jerusalem and the area around it, not the authorities, so no level says "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (R as at L and B)
decisions.reason: English Readable says "leading priests" for young readers. French "les chefs des prêtres" is already plain, so it is used at every level, as throughout John.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" (L, B); "các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu" (R)
decisions.reason: The chief priests, named as in 11:47.

decisions.choice: "старшие священники"
decisions.reason: The style guide's term (section 6): the plural "первосвященники" would blur the one high priest with the leading priests.

decisions.choice: "уходили от них" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable say whom the people were leaving: the authorities (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the open verb.

decisions.choice: "祭司長たちから離れて" (B, R); "去って行き" (L)
alternatives: "出かけて行き" (going out to Bethany)
decisions.reason: As the English does, Balanced and Readable follow m1 and say whom the people were leaving; Literal keeps the open "going away". The choice is uncertain (m1 has a footnote).
